leads.work: Real-time desk sends daily short/long position notices to the shift group by hand: MW, price, book, delivery point, and which desk to check prices with
leads.why: The same kind of email goes out almost every day, from Bill and from Kate, with per-book volumes and prices typed in by hand. The content could come straight from position or schedule data.

leads.work: El Paso Electric (EPE) lending/parking deals and the daily El Paso model vs CARP report tie-out, with monthly settlement checkout and dispute handling
leads.why: Last month's checkout took 5 days, and disputes with EPE are growing. There are repeated reminders about the CARP tie-out, unit dispatch order and the reconciliation model. A trader error (selling below $15 without ramping down Four Corners) happened more than once. Deal-entry steps are given out fresh each day.

leads.work: Manual Colstrip cut procedure: index buy, BPA transmission deal, zeroing and linking deals in Enpower, then entering cuts in the Lotus Notes Cuts database, a forum note and emails
leads.why: A 10-step manual procedure that was revised after only one day. The Lotus Notes cuts entry is described as 'the most time consuming portion.' It runs again every time Colstrip goes down.

leads.work: Congestion relief revenue and ISO charges: daily emails to Volume Mgmt/Risk with MW × price, checking against the CAISO flash, a daily exposure tally, adding dummy Enpower deals to flatten the variance report, and month-end true-up
leads.why: Revenue is announced by email nearly every day, and items missing from the flash are chased by hand. Deals are entered 'only for the sake of the report.' The August true-up variances were reconciled by hand over several emails.

leads.work: EOL hourly trade volume entered by hand into Enpower/CAPS: the night shift computes weighted-average interdesk strips, inc sheets are kept up every hour, and book-to-book transfers are booked by hand
leads.why: 530+ EOL trades in 8 days strained the systems and the staff. Standards were reissued several times. EOL trades were not captured properly, causing delays for other groups. The night shift averages prices by hand to build single interdesk deals.

leads.work: Bloomberg broker trades matched by hand against Enpower, and broker fees assigned by hand
leads.why: Settlements sent a spreadsheet of unmatched August Bloomberg deals (Aug 1–22) that missed the two-day grace period. Fee-entry errors inflate brokerage costs, and Kate suggests simply multiplying $15 by the trade count.

leads.work: Resolving counterparty settlement disputes by requesting and listening to trading tapes (EPE/SRP, MPC Montana imbalance)
leads.why: The MPC March imbalance had gone back and forth for 5 months. Several sets of tapes were requested, and the tapes often lack time, point or price. Tape access goes through one person.

leads.work: Cell phone usage monitoring and overage billing for the RT group
leads.why: Repeated overages, about $20k spent by June. Bills are checked by hand per person, users are moved between plans, and a new chargeback policy has to be enforced every month.

leads.work: Misrouted mail to the wrong 'Bill Williams' (Portland III vs Sweden/Houston namesakes), with replies asking to be removed from lists
leads.why: At least 10 messages had to be forwarded on or answered with 'wrong person', covering EOL loadshapes, Bloomberg deals, badge access, admin lists and showers. This points to a directory or address-book problem.

leads.work: Turret, handset and phone provisioning requests, and IT access changes for the RT desk (directory restriction, schedule crawler)
leads.why: Handsets keep going missing or breaking, and requests for turrets and phones repeat through IT. Access lists are maintained by hand by email.

leads.work: Requesting Enpower trader IDs and desk access for new traders and interns through Global Counterparty
leads.why: Kate writes 'once again in need of a new trader ID.' Access was incomplete (an Originator ID was missing and a trader had been left off), so follow-ups were needed.

leads.work: Service-customer reporting done by hand: Grays Harbor generator output to BPA, the EES ancillary spin dispatch log and next-morning sheet to EES Settlements, and fax submissions to the Alberta Power Pool for Enron Canada
leads.why: Recurring daily reporting through spreadsheets, phone calls and faxes. BPA says its own automatic recording system is coming. The RT desk has no working digital certificate, so Alberta submissions have to be faxed.

leads.work: CAISO adjustment-bid tiering entered by hand, plus ADS dispatch decline research
leads.why: A rule-based bid tier (values must increase monotonically, at most 10 bids) is typed in by hand, and errors are costly. Revenue was lost by not adjust-bidding. The ISO raised an 82% decline count that needed investigation.

leads.work: Gas settlements researching payment and deal discrepancies with AEP/HPL after the sale (missing deals, wrong counterparties, overpayments, unbooked invoices)
leads.why: Many cases from one analyst: Killam had no May deal, Conoco Big Cowboy was overpaid about $1.5M per month, Coral invoices had no deals behind them, and the TGLO July deal could not be found. Each one needs digging through Path Manager, Sitara audit logs and AEP contacts.

leads.work: TGLO gas-for-crude intercompany deals (HPLC/ENA/EGM) booked month by month by hand
leads.why: A complicated procedure (zeroing prices, demand-fee tickets) was completed only for Jan–Feb, so March–May are outstanding, and someone reversed a correction. It recurs monthly.

leads.work: Correcting Sitara volumes and pricing for Guadalupe Power swing/baseload deals from settlement spreadsheets
leads.why: Settlements send spreadsheets each month, and logistics re-enters volumes and prices, with typos (50,000 entered instead of 30,000). Sitara reportedly cannot handle average-GD+0.02 pricing, so the price is calculated by hand.

leads.work: Prior-period cleanup: bridgeback errors from late pathing on expired deals, and new deal tickets to clear old (1999) inter-pipeline pool balances
leads.why: Requests go back and forth, with follow-up emails resent after weeks. Deal tickets are created one at a time to clear balances from 1999. Actualization errors such as TUFCO volume at 0 are routed between groups.

leads.work: Approval workflows: meter and pipe code setup, application access requests, expense reports, and the OPM hours survey split
leads.why: These are routine approvals routed by email or AR system to one manager. The hours survey had to be followed up by hand because the system did not prompt for the percentage split.

leads.work: Monthly admin-assistant roster verification by email (titles, extensions, supervisors)
leads.why: Explicitly monthly. A spreadsheet goes to about 35 people for confirmation, and some recipients are wrong.

leads.work: Month-end close freeze and scheduler cutoffs, plus coordinating system maintenance windows
leads.why: Changes to the close schedule caused confusion among schedulers. Reports are picked up by hand. The maintenance window was negotiated across about 20 people.

leads.work: Unwinding and re-explaining old profit-share annuities (the LP deal) between books at month end
leads.why: Annuity routing across ST-NW, Whourly, LT-NW and L-Pac had to be rebuilt months later from Bill's spreadsheet, and the request was urgent at month end.

leads.work: Recurring management admin: budget planning spreadsheets, PEP reviews, interview scheduling, shift schedule changes, and night discussion-note quality
leads.why: Budget worksheets are revised by hand. Review forms and ranking follow-ups are handled one by one. Shift swaps are tracked by email and on paper.

leads.work: Setting up EOL hourly products: loadshape legal review, pop-up text, and customer filter requests
leads.why: Several rounds of back-and-forth, made worse by misrouting. Customers asked for an hourly-product filter.

leads.work: Weather info spreadsheet and intranet page maintained by hand for traders
leads.why: Kate is building a spreadsheet and web page that she would update herself. A similar intranet effort is under way separately with Fundamentals, so work may be duplicated.

leads.work: Daily nomination confirmations from Pace Global by spreadsheet
leads.why: An emailed nomination spreadsheet has to be confirmed by hand, with ongoing updates.

leads.work: Phone and tie-line dial-string changes that require users to reprogram auto-dial buttons by hand; ERMS RUNM application migration
leads.why: A firm-wide change makes every user reprogram buttons, fax machines and conference phones. The ERMS migration requires users to test and reboot themselves.
